statement: In the Neophyte grade the step is a short advance of the left foot; the signs are the Saluting Sign (leaning forward with both arms outstretched, as if groping for light), answered by the Sign of Silence (left forefinger on the lips); the grip is made foot to foot, the hands failing once to meet and then touching only the fingers; and the grand word Har-Par-Krat is whispered mouth to ear in syllables.
verification_notes: Checked against the Internet Archive text of Volume Two (1938) on 2026-11-04. The ritual says the password changes every equinox, so that members who have left do not know it, and leaves it blank.

statement: The penalty in the Neophyte obligation was changed: the version printed in 1909 calls down a deadly current of will from the chiefs of the Order that would strike the oath-breaker dead or paralysed, while the Stella Matutina version printed in 1938 sets expulsion for perjury and submission, by the candidate's own consent, to a stream of power set in motion by the Order's Divine Guardians.
verification_notes: Checked against the Internet Archive text of Volume Two (1938) on 2026-11-04. Also checked against The Equinox I(2). Each source attests one wording; the change itself is shown by comparing them, and the 1909 text's footnote also mentions a softened later wording.

statement: Elders may take disciplinary action only on a confession, the testimony of two or three credible eyewitnesses to the same incident, or strong circumstantial evidence testified to by at least two witnesses (the two-witness rule). Without that, an accused person who denies the allegation continues to be viewed as innocent and the matter is left in Jehovah's hands.
